# LZ4 - Extremely fast compression

LZ4 is lossless compression algorithm,
providing compression speed > 500 MB/s per core,
scalable with multi-cores CPU.
It features an extremely fast decoder,
with speed in multiple GB/s per core,
typically reaching RAM speed limits on multi-core systems.

Speed can be tuned dynamically, selecting an "acceleration" factor
which trades compression ratio for faster speed.
On the other end, a high compression derivative, LZ4_HC, is also provided,
trading CPU time for improved compression ratio.
All versions feature the same decompression speed.

LZ4 is also compatible with dictionary compression,
which can dramatically improve compression performance on small files.

## Command Line Usage

The `lz4` command line tool provides file compression and decompression:

### Basic Usage

```bash
lz4 [OPTIONS] [-|INPUT-FILE] <OUTPUT-FILE>
```

- `lz4 file1 file2` - compress file1 into file2
- `lz4 -d file.lz4` - decompress file.lz4
- `lz4 -z file` - force compression (creates file.lz4)
- `lz4cat file.lz4` - decompress to stdout (equivalent to `lz4 -dcfm`)
- `unlz4` - equivalent to `lz4 -d`

### Key Options

- `-z`, `--compress` - Force compression
- `-d`, `--decompress` - Decompress
- `-t`, `--test` - Test compressed file integrity
- `-c` - Force write to stdout
- `-m` - Multiple files mode
- `-r` - Recursive mode (directories)
- `-B#` - Block size (4=64KB, 5=256KB, 6=1MB, 7=4MB)
- `-#` - Compression level (1-9 for standard, 10-12 for HC)
- `--rm` - Remove source files after successful compression/decompression
- `-k`, `--keep` - Keep source files (default)
- `-f`, `--force` - Overwrite output without prompting
- `-q`, `--quiet` - Suppress warnings

### Examples

```bash
# Compress a file
lz4 myfile myfile.lz4

# Decompress a file
lz4 -d myfile.lz4 myfile

# Compress multiple files
lz4 -m file1 file2 file3

# High compression mode
lz4 -9 myfile myfile.lz4

# Test file integrity
lz4 -t myfile.lz4
```

### File Format

LZ4 uses the `.lz4` file extension. Multiple `.lz4` files can be concatenated
and will decompress as a single stream.

### Performance Characteristics

- **Compression speed**: Typically > 500 MB/s per core
- **Decompression speed**: Multiple GB/s per core (often RAM-bound)
- **Compression ratio**: Moderate (focuses on speed over ratio)
- **LZ4_HC mode**: Better compression ratio at the cost of compression speed

### Notes

- By default, source files are preserved after compression/decompression
- When input is stdin or output is stdout, data is streamed
- The tool automatically detects `.lz4` files and defaults to decompression
- Use `-q` to suppress progress indicators when scripting

- `-z`, `--compress` - Force compression

- `-c` - Force write to stdout

- `-r` - Recursive mode (directories)

lz4 myfile myfile.lz4
